# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (best overall, clip-on).** Runner's World picks these as best overall, and WIRED likes the clear sound and physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run. They list at $199 (down from $299), but only have IPX4 water resistance and about 7 hours of battery. Runner's World also says Bose has a new pair coming within a month, so you may want to wait. [Buy links in Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (best bone conduction).** This is the best choice if awareness matters most. It has 12 hours of battery, IP55 water resistance, and physical controls. The neckband can interfere with long hair and winter hats, and WIRED found the sound less clear than the older OpenRun. Prices vary a lot by retailer: $180 on Amazon, but $125 at Best Buy, REI, Walmart, and Lowe's in the listings. [WIRED review with buy links](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)

**Shokz OpenDots 2 (best for long runs).** It lasts 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and is IP57 rated, so rain isn't a concern. It costs $200. [WIRED's guide with buy links](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Nothing Ear (Open) (SoundGuys' top pick overall and for running).** SoundGuys praises its bass and EQ controls, and it has IP54 sweat resistance. It was $99 on Amazon (MSRP $149). [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Soundcore AeroFit 2 (best value).** It has IP55 protection and long battery life. SoundGuys lists it at $79.99 on Amazon, while Soundcore's own store shows $129.99. That's a big gap, so check both. Dealectric says code AFSC20 takes 20% off full-price items, which would make it $104, but the code isn't valid on sale items, so Amazon may be cheaper. [Buy at Soundcore's store via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2) (affiliate link: Dealectric earns a commission, and the price is the same for you.)

**JLab Flex Open (budget).** It's a low-risk way to try clip-ons at around $40–50, though the sound has less bass and detail than the pricier pairs. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

## Quick pick
- **Max awareness, heavy sweat or rain:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2
- **Best sound in a clip-on:** Bose Ultra Open (consider waiting for the new model)
- **Marathon-length battery:** Shokz OpenDots 2
- **Best value:** Soundcore AeroFit 2 or Nothing Ear (Open)
- **Unsure about open-ear:** JLab Flex Open

Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic. Open-ear designs help with awareness but don't guarantee safety.
